owner_objective: Find and repair every reason why the locally configured Binance API key/secret cannot progress Hixton through the controlled 1x50-USDC trial and then normal 250-USDC Live. Cloud remains key-free and order-free; it must prove all code, state, UI and runtime gates up to the local authenticated boundary.

acceptance.controlled_trial: A fresh local authenticated account preflight can arm exactly one 50-USDC trial without immediately submitting an old signal; the next fresh valid signal can progress through entry, fill, bot-owned ledger, strategy exit, sell fill and reconciliation.
acceptance.production_live: Only after a completed/reconciled controlled trial can normal saved max_capital_usdc Live become eligible; default 250 USDC maps to CAPITAL-V1-2X50PCT, two ranked-repeat tranches of 125 USDC.
acceptance.ownership: Pre-existing Binance balances are baseline-only and may never be sold unless tied to a Hixton-owned position/order ledger.
acceptance.runtime_identity: UI, backend, running process, strategy, source and allocator identity are explicitly checked; stale runtime blocks new entries and must surface a precise remediation.
acceptance.cloud_boundary: No GitHub/cloud job may read private Binance credentials or place real/testnet orders.

A01.objective: Trace every documented and coded prerequisite for controlled 1x50 trial and later 250-USDC Live. Identify circular, obsolete or contradictory gates and stale documentation.

A02.objective: Verify strategy/backtest signal semantics permit the trial to wait for the next fresh valid signal and never replay an old signal. Identify signal-frequency, candle-close or timestamp conditions that can look like a broken trial.

A03.objective: Audit Paper/Live parity, persistent state, account baseline, bot-owned ledger and every trial-state transition. Find stale armed/failed/completed states or ownership conflicts that can block a new 1x50 trial.

A04.objective: Reproduce the operator flow in the shipped UI: credential status, account check, trial arm/start, error display and later Live enable. Find false disabled states, stale frontend bundle or missing confirmations.

A05.objective: Detect stale running processes, source/version drift, restart requirements, stale market data and scheduler inactivity that could leave a configured system unable to consume the next trial signal.

A06.objective: Reproduce the full failure path from configured credentials to controlled-trial eligibility with fake/auth-boundary tests. Extend the failure matrix for duplicate submit, timeout, retry, restart, budget change, stale version, EXIT_ONLY and circular gate failures. Repair integration defects.

A07.objective: Audit authenticated-preflight implementation and current Binance Spot USDC requirements: API permission/status handling, IP restriction errors, balance, filters, precision and reconciliation assumptions. Never use private credentials in cloud.

A08.objective: Audit every strategy/risk/capital/safety gate that can block the 50-USDC trial or subsequent Live: emergency stop, entry pause, daily loss pause, open bot positions, cash, version/source/allocator mismatch and 10x250 research separation.

A09.objective: Independently QA the repaired exact commit only after A10 has complete fresh evidence. Reject any mixed-commit, stale, mocked-as-real or incomplete Live-readiness claim.

A10.objective: Act as dispatcher and problem router. Build the exact blocker chain UI -> credentials -> authenticated preflight -> baseline/ledger -> trial state -> runtime/version -> fresh signal -> risk/capital -> order -> fill/reconciliation -> trial completion -> Live eligibility. Assign every defect to a named specialist and require a new pinned rerun after repairs.

A11.objective: Audit the complete repair process and A10 itself. Reject ownerless blockers, stale/mixed evidence, circular approvals and any claim that a real 50-USDC Binance roundtrip happened in cloud.
